items.t: Balance shaft gear wear (check engine light, P0016/P0017)
items.job: Replace balance shaft, timing chain and sprockets
items.note: Owners report dealer quotes of about $4,000 to $9,300; some paid $7,000. Mercedes sometimes shared the cost as goodwill. A used later engine is a cheaper alternative some owners choose.

items.t: 7-speed automatic harsh shifts or limp mode (valve body)
items.job: Replace transmission valve body/conductor plate and program
items.note: Owners report about $1,200 to $1,800. A reconditioned or rebuilt transmission costs about $5,600 to $6,600 or more.

items.t: Air suspension (Airmatic) sagging or "too low" warning
items.job: Replace one Airmatic air spring or strut
items.note: Owners paid about $220 to $400 for a single air spring and $1,100 to $2,000 for a pair of struts.

items.t: Air suspension compressor failure
items.note: Owners report $1,100 to $1,500.

items.t: Camshaft adjuster solenoid failure or oil leak
items.note: One owner paid $450 for a single magnet; replacing several with sensors ran about $1,300.

items.t: Intake manifold cracking or runner flap failure
items.note: Owners report about $2,000 to $2,500 at a shop.

items.t: Power steering pump noise or leaks
items.job: Replace power steering pump and reservoir
items.note: Owners report $450 to $830; one paid $3,400 when more parts were needed.

items.t: Power steering rack leaking
items.note: Owners report about $1,050 to $4,800.

items.t: Front differential failure (4MATIC)
items.note: Owners reported about $3,000 to $3,500 out of warranty; one dealer quoted $4,500.

items.t: Front axle shaft (CV joint) wear
items.note: Owner-reported costs range from about $800 to $2,300 including other work.

items.t: Stuck in Park or shifter faults
items.job: Replace shift module or transmission control unit and program
items.note: Owners report about $1,175 to $1,280.

items.t: Rear lights failing or "substitute lights" message
items.job: Repair tail light wiring or replace light module
items.note: Owners were quoted about $200 to $250 for wiring and $800 to $950 to replace a control unit.

items.t: Stalling from fuel pump or its wiring burning
items.job: Replace fuel pump (and repair wiring if burned)
items.note: RepairPal estimates $1,326 to $1,736 for the pump; one owner with burned wiring expected about $4,000.

items.t: Power liftgate or tailgate latch failure
items.note: RepairPal estimates about $1,060 to $1,100 for the actuator; owners paid $250 to $500 for latch repairs.

items.t: Door lock actuator failure
items.note: Owners report about $600 to $1,000.

items.t: Dead main or auxiliary battery and electrical faults
items.note: Owners paid $625 to $1,700 for both batteries. Replacing SAM modules as well cost one owner about $4,000.

items.t: Thermostat failure (no heat or slow warm-up)
items.note: Owners report about $650 to $940 including other small jobs.

items.t: ABS and stability warning from wheel speed sensor
items.note: Owners paid about $200 to $335 per sensor.

items.t: Creaking front suspension (ball joints)
items.job: Replace front control arm/ball joint and align
items.note: RepairPal estimates control arm bushing replacement at about $515 to $640.

items.t: Oil seeping from back of cylinder heads
items.note: One owner paid $943 together with a thermostat replacement.

items.t: Oil pan gasket leak
items.job: Replace engine oil pan or gasket
items.note: RepairPal estimates about $1,280 to $1,670.

items.t: Turbodiesel turbocharger oil leak or failure
items.note: Owners report about $5,000 to $6,500.

items.t: Transmission oil cooler line leak (diesel)
items.note: One owner paid $932 for both lines.

items.t: A/C blowing warm (compressor or leak)
items.note: Owners paid $500 to $1,200; RepairPal estimates an evaporator at $1,800 to $2,900.

items.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensors or exhaust manifold
items.note: One owner paid $800 for sensors; another paid $4,000 for an exhaust manifold plus sensors.
